overview: This Senate resolution supports naming October 24 to October 31, 2026, "Bat Week." It highlights the role bats play in eating crop-damaging insects, pollinating plants and spreading seeds, noting an estimate that they save U.S. farmers more than $3.7 billion a year in pest control. It describes white-nose syndrome, a fungal disease that has killed millions of hibernating bats and spread to 41 states, and the work of federal agencies such as the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and U.S. Geological Survey, along with states, tribes and universities, to track bat populations and fight the disease. The resolution encourages Bat Week events and says the Senate intends to keep working to conserve bats and defeat white-nose syndrome. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say bats quietly provide major benefits to farming and ecosystems, and public awareness helps build support for protecting them from a deadly disease.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for bat conservation or disease research.
